verdict.rationale: Moss is a semantic search runtime, so replicating data across nodes or zones for high availability is a fair question for it. The evidence only describes local indexing that syncs to the cloud, hydrating from the cloud with hot-swaps, and serving a disk-cached snapshot when the cloud is unreachable. These are client caching and resilience behaviors, not documented multi-node or multi-zone replication, and no consistency model is described anywhere.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can replicate data across nodes or zones for high availability with a documented consistency model
